changes: Removed the 1 MiB execFileSync default that made DONE metadata silently unreliable, and shipped CHK-004 as outcome B. packages/main/src/core/done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts now passes METADATA_BLOB_READ_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES = 33554432 on all ten git read sites; the bare catches that swallowed ENOBUFS are replaced by typed results that distinguish absent from unreadable, with describeContentReadFailure reading stderr only and describeDiagnosticStreamFailure allowed to include hook stdout, both capped. packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts gains boundPersistedValidationEvidence: it builds the record a write site would write, serialises it in the format core/store.ts uses, counts those bytes, and drives a staged reduction against that count rather than an estimate, returning one of unmodified, reduced, verdict_only or refused; snapshotPersistedRecord returns JSON.parse of the measured text so the returned graph carries no own toJSON, getter or Proxy trap. All three write sites in packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts refuse to write when withinBound is false or the record is null. An advisory fires at 25 percent of the read ceiling and the bound sits at 75 percent, both derived from the ceiling rather than chosen beside it. Two regression harnesses ship and are registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands: packages/main/tests/red/red-b3434-blob-buffer-ceiling.mjs, which embeds the pre-fix helper verbatim so it fails against the old code, and packages/main/src/tasks/validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.ts. What did NOT ship is a guarantee that the measured number equals the bytes StoryStore writes; docs/requirements/decisions/validation-evidence-artifact-growth.md records why, with transcripts, and names the change that will provide one.
usage: Nothing to invoke. done_prepare and the DONE gate read blobs through the raised ceiling automatically, and lattice validate bounds test-evidence.json on every run through the same code path. An operator sees the difference in two places: a blob above 33554432 bytes now fails loudly as unreadable with the captured byte count in the message instead of returning null, and validate prints a sizing advisory once the serialised artifact passes 8388608 bytes, naming the measured size and the limit, worded so it cannot be read as a failure. When the artifact cannot be brought under 25165824 bytes the evidence write is refused with a structured failure naming the size and the bound, rather than written and left to break the next metadata commit.
expectedOutcome: A tracked file larger than 1 MiB is hashed correctly rather than silently skipped; a file larger than the new ceiling fails with a diagnostic instead of a null; the aggregate evidence artifact is reduced to fit rather than growing until it breaks the metadata commit; and the growth dimension CHK-004 names, the number of configured validate commands serialised into test-evidence.json, is covered.
actualTranscript: Real git blobs, measured by the behavior lane at the shipping revision: a 5 MiB blob reads correctly with sha256 matching an independently computed digest; a 40 MiB blob fails as unreadable with 'ENOBUFS: output exceeded the 33554432-byte read ceiling; 33562624 bytes were captured before the ceiling and discarded'; a missing path is absent with real git text. Sizing, from validation-evidence-buffer-smoke: the 100-command shape this repository actually has measures 2520038 bytes, unmodified, within_budget, output byte-identical to the pre-story serialisation; 400 commands of all-quote output measure 38878838 bytes unbounded, past the read ceiling, and 19617036 after reduction; 300 commands by 100000 chars reduce to 148987 bytes with 250200 detail lines replaced by counted markers; 180000 heterogeneous detail entries reduce to 16029894 bytes keeping 180001 detail lines, so a reducible artifact is reduced rather than discarded for a stub; a 200000-entry verificationCoverage is refused at 53489880 bytes and nothing is written. The incident artifact that motivated this story measured 1369692 bytes at 100 entries against a 1048576-byte ceiling, after the command list grew from 56 to 100 in one day, and it blocked every REVIEW to TEST transition in the repository. Full suite at the shipping revision: 97 of 97 commands pass, verification coverage gap 0, test-evidence.json result PASS.
outcomeDiff: Matches on the metadata ceiling, the diagnostics and the reduction. Diverges on one thing, and it is the reason CHK-004 shipped as outcome B rather than outcome A: the bound is a measurement, not a guarantee. Four routes by which the measured number and the bytes on disk can come apart are open, filed and deferred with transcripts. The serialisation format is duplicated from core/store.ts rather than shared with it and the smoke's apparent pin is self-referential, so a format change there moves both copies together and every assertion keeps passing (B-3434:F-033; demonstrated at 158 expected, 158 measured, 168 written). JSON.parse returns objects on a live Object.prototype, so an inherited toJSON defeats the snapshot even for a plain object literal (cross-vendor finding; 67 bytes reported within bound, 31457342 on disk). finish() takes record and fileBytes as independent trusted parameters rather than re-deriving one from the other (B-3434:F-035). The F-029 source check is blind to in-place mutation of the record between the gate and the write (B-3434:F-037; reproduced with one line, no cast, zero new tsc errors, smoke unaffected). None is reachable from real input: every production buildRecord closure builds a fresh plain object literal with no toJSON, getter or Proxy in its graph. All are recorded in the decision document with the change that removes them.
limitations: The guarantee is deferred, not delivered, and the reason is structural rather than remaining effort: it needs a writer-owned canonical boundary in packages/main/src/core/store.ts that serialises, measures and writes the exact measured bytes, and that file is outside this story's allowedModify. Nine review rounds on this side of the seam could not build the property. B-3434:F-036 is also deferred: the snapshot is applied uniformly across every measurement including the reduction loop's discarded candidates, costing smoke wall-clock 9.9s to about 18.5s for no benefit, since the terminal call re-snapshots independently. It is sequenced after the boundary rather than independent of it, because the number the search phase keeps must come from the boundary's measure-only entry point rather than from a second copy of the format. The decision document is the work order and names all of it.
pitfalls: Three worth carrying forward. First, the recurring defect this story is a case study in: a claim in prose wider than what the code enforces, which appeared in eight forms across twelve rounds, where each fix's own new comments introduced the next instance. The converging answer was to make the property derived rather than remembered, and where that was impossible, to delete the claim rather than narrow it. Second, cross-vendor review earned its cost here rather than satisfying a policy: five genuine codex exec reviews ran, and in four consecutive rounds codex found a real defect that four Claude lanes at the same revision had missed, including one in a correction that had just been written to fix the previous one. Because cross-host findings are filed under main, which has no registered reviewer lane, none of them gated anything until a Claude lane reproduced each by execution and refiled it under its own lane; that gap is filed as follow-up work. Third, two operational facts. This story's own RED harness had never run in the standing suite for twelve rounds; only the full validate run caught it, through the repository's own registration guard, because every checklist selector bound to direct invocation of the harness and so 'the regression passes' and 'the regression is wired into the suite' stayed silently distinct claims. And the standing suite now takes about 884 seconds against a 900000 ms default watchdog, so the one successful full run needed LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS raised to 2400000; that variable is baked into effectiveEnvironmentDigest, so it was set only on the standalone validate and deliberately not on any gate command. Both are filed as separate follow-up work.
